summary: Prepar3D and FSX support, X-Plane 11 navigation data, and a map that wraps around the world without a black edge.
releaseNotes: Prepar3D v4 to v6: Stratos finds Prepar3D's own SimConnect library and connects to it automatically.
FSX: tried through the same SimConnect connection. FSX is 32-bit, so this depends on it accepting the 64-bit connection.
X-Plane 11: the bridge now finds X-Plane 11 installs for SIDs, STARs, ILS and the IFR charts, as it does for X-Plane 12.
Settings shows which simulator SimConnect is connected to: MSFS, Prepar3D or FSX.
Zooming out or panning past the date line no longer leaves a black side: map tiles, radar and FAA charts repeat around the world.
Aircraft, airports, the route and your own aircraft repeat on every visible copy of the world, and clicking a copy selects the real one.
X-Plane 11 ILS courses show the true course instead of a wrong 360° magnetic.
The top-bar Go Premium button is gone. Stratos is free, and a Support Stratos button appears only when a support page is set.
